TRACE review materials

From scientific questions to inspectable evidence.

TRACE is a multi-agent workflow for seismic research. It turns a scientific request into a sequence of plans, tools, executable analysis, checks, and evidence-linked results.

See how it works v Explore the cases
The central idea

An agent is not just a chatbot that writes code. It is a controlled loop that plans, executes, inspects, revises, and records scientific work.

104 benchmark tasks
3 evaluated models
2 earthquake case studies
25,646 validated Sanriku events

01 / The idea

What does "agent" mean here?

A scientific agent is a system that can move through a research workflow. The language model supplies reasoning and code generation, while the surrounding workflow supplies tools, files, validation rules, and a persistent record of what happened.

In plain language

You give TRACE a question such as "How did seismicity evolve after the Ridgecrest mainshocks?" TRACE breaks that question into workable stages, writes the analysis needed for each stage, runs it, checks the outputs, and keeps the evidence that supports the final interpretation.

For a reviewer

The public release exposes the case entry scripts, generated analysis code, parameters, outputs, reports, state records, and execution trajectories. Each layer can be inspected independently and traced back to the scientific question.

03 / Scientific cases

What do the outputs mean?

The case studies show the workflow operating on real seismological questions. The point is not only to produce a figure, but to connect data preparation, computational choices, diagnostics, and interpretation.

Ridgecrest / 2019

How did the sequence reorganize between Mw 6.4 and Mw 7.1?

TRACE constructs a waveform-to-catalog workflow, then uses the relocated catalog to examine branching, fault alignment, activation, migration, and the transition between the two mainshocks.

Released result 84,474-event relocated catalog with time-windowed spatial evidence and report-linked figures
View Ridgecrest materials ->
Sanriku / 2025-2026

How can a regional catalog support sequence-scale interpretation?

TRACE prepares, relocates, validates, and analyzes the Sanriku catalog, then follows event-centered activation, event relationships, spatial-depth structure, mechanisms, and migration-related patterns.

Released result 25,646-event validated catalog with manuscript-aligned repeating-earthquake products
View Sanriku materials ->
From waveform to catalog

Specialized tools remain visible inside the agent workflow.

Phase picking, association, relocation, correlation, and statistical analysis are not hidden behind a single score. Each stage leaves an inspectable computational product.

From catalog to evidence

Scientific meaning comes from linked comparisons.

Spatial expansion, event-centered activation, and migration-like patterns are interpreted alongside controls, scope definitions, and the limits of the available observations.

04 / Why it matters

The result is a chain of evidence, not a single answer.

TRACE is useful when the scientific task is too open-ended for a single fixed script, but the conclusion still needs to be inspected like ordinary research.

A

For the workflow

The benchmark asks whether an agent can carry out concrete scientific operations and longer chains of operations with recoverable records.

B

For the evidence

The case records make the path from request to result visible: plans, code, parameters, figures, reports, and trajectories stay connected.

C

For seismology

The outputs turn large earthquake catalogs into structured evidence about sequence organization, activation, relocation, and repeating events.

05 / Evidence trail

Start with the question. End at the file.

The website is the explanation layer. The public release remains the source of truth for scripts, parameters, outputs, reports, and execution records.
